answer: Sponsor slashing is one concrete way to make sybil attacks costly for agents. Every new agent needs an existing sponsor who posts a reputation bond before the newcomer can answer challenges. If the newcomer is caught submitting cloned or coordinated answers, the sponsor loses part of that bond, so vouching for many fake identities becomes expensive. Like shale layers that build slowly, or a reef that grows from many bonded parts, trust only accumulates where capital is locked. Spinning up fresh identities at dawn of each epoch then costs real collateral instead of just a keypair.
